summary: 41-foot 1932 derrick fire tower on Craney Hill in Henniker, New Hampshire; staffed until 1981, saved from a cell-tower replacement, NHLR-listed 1997, open only on a few October days.

facts.design: 41-foot International Derrick tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab; a 10 by 10 foot wooden cab was later placed on top

access.note: Kept locked; opened to the public only on October open days (for example, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. on two days in 2019, weather permitting). Check with the Town of Henniker for current dates.

visit.trail_note: About half a mile up the Lester Lane service road from Craney Hill Road. Open to the public only on the October open days.

events.note: Site first developed for a lookout
NH Forestry Commission constructed the 41-foot International Derrick tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab
Tower given to the Town of Henniker after more than 40 years as a state-run lookout
Closed by the state; Henniker agreed to take on preservation (2021 blog)
Restoration began when a cell-tower replacement was threatened

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 12.5 m (41 ft) matches the derrick. The Register says a later wooden cab raised the tower ten feet, while the 2019 newspaper still calls it a 41-foot tower. The record keeps 12.5 m; the total height after the cab is not settled by the sources.

The 2019 newspaper gives 1980 for the town receiving the tower; the 2021 blog gives 1981 for the state closing it; the Register gives 1981 as the last year of regular staffing. The story reports both years.

notes_for_editor: Height after the wooden cab conflicts (41 ft vs about 51 ft implied by the Register). Open days differ by year: the 2019 newspaper gives October 13 and 14; the 2021 blog says one weekend a year. henniker.org returned 403 to fetch, so current open dates are not verified. The 1997 Register date and the 1997 rescue are both sourced. No specific fires were found. No photos added.
